producer_judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same grain, same rank 1) in Strand 2 Algebra but in different sub-strands: B5.2.3.1.1 (Variables and Equations) asks pupils to express a given problem as an equation with the unknown represented by a letter/variable, while B5.2.1.1.1 (Patterns and Relationships) asks pupils to extend a given pattern with and without concrete materials and explain how each element differs from the preceding one. Their LCs confirm distinct skills (symbolic representation of an unknown vs. pattern extension and element-difference explanation), and the token/trigram overlap is only on function words ('a', 'given', 'the') plus a shared code prefix, which is not semantic evidence. There is nonetheless genuine algebraic coherence: describing how successive pattern elements change is the generalizing reasoning that complements representing unknown quantities symbolically, so they reinforce each other within the same grade's algebra work. No substantive same-rank evidence establishes that proficiency in either specifically supports success in the other, so the symmetric relation is used. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all context nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, including a merged BASIC 5 Grade organizer.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators (same statement-type grain) on efficient multi-digit multiplication. The first (B4.1.2.3.1, BASIC 4, rank 0) is 'Multiply multi-digit numbers efficiently' under Content Standard B4.1.2.3 'multiplication (2 or 3-digit by 1-digit)' in Strand 1 NUMBER / Sub-strand 2 Number Operations. The second (B5.1.2.2.1, BASIC 5, rank 1) extends the same efficient multiplication skill to multiplying multi-digit numbers by 2-digit multipliers, with its own Content Standard B5.1.2.2 covering 2 or 3-digit by 2 or 3-digit multiplication. This is substantive extension of multiplier size rather than generic repetition, and fluency with single-digit-multiplier multi-digit multiplication supports success with two-digit multipliers; direction runs lower-to-higher BASIC 4 to BASIC 5. Note that the second endpoint and its parent carry unresolved-ancestry warnings, so no positive hierarchy evidence was taken from a framework-root fallback; the judgment rests on the trustworthy statement text, codes, and resolved grade coordinates. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which was not reconstructed.
